title: X5 · Write it, then find it
description: The order was written two minutes ago and has since been flushed. Support needs it now. Trace the write and the read on one board.

problemStatement.overview:
**14:00:** order-processor writes `PUT order:88213 → status=paid`.

**14:01:** the memtable fills up and is flushed. order:88213 is now in `000913.sst`, the newest of 212 SSTables.

**14:02:** a customer calls support. Support runs `GET order:88213`.

Kavya (from X4) is back: *"OK, I get writes. But with 212 files on disk, how does a read find one key without opening all of them?"*

Draw both halves on one board: three write steps, then three read steps.
problemStatement.yourTask: Trace order:88213 from the PUT into an SSTable, then trace the GET that finds it.
yourTaskSteps: Steps 1–3: the write, down to an SSTable.
Steps 4–6: the read, from memory down to one disk block.
One optional block sits in the read path.
hints: Reads look where the newest data lives first.
A Bloom filter can say “definitely not here”. It can never say “definitely here”.
problemStatement.moat: Campaign: unlockAfter x4. Chain: wal-append → memtable-insert → flush-sstable → read-memtables → read-bloom → read-block. Optional: block-cache between read-bloom and read-block.

platformSpec.passMessage: Kavya: “So a read checks memory, asks each file’s Bloom filter newest-first, and only opens one block. Nice.”

pieces.title: Append to the WAL and fsync
Insert into the memtable, reply OK
pieces.blurb: The write is readable and acknowledged.

pieces.title: Freeze and flush to 000913.sst
pieces.blurb: At 64 MB the memtable is frozen and written out as the newest SSTable.

pieces.title: GET checks the memtables first
pieces.blurb: Active, then frozen. The newest data lives here. Miss: order:88213 was already flushed.

pieces.title: Ask each SSTable’s Bloom filter, newest first
pieces.blurb: 000913.sst says “maybe”. The other files it asks say “definitely not”, so they’re skipped without touching disk.

pieces.title: Check the block cache
pieces.blurb: If the block is already in memory from a recent read, skip the disk entirely.

pieces.title: Use the sparse index to read one block
pieces.blurb: Binary-search 000913.sst’s index, read the single block that covers order:88213, and return status=paid.

pieces.title: Search SSTables oldest first
pieces.trapIfPlaced: You might return a stale version. The newest file wins, so search newest first.

pieces.title: Scan the WAL for the key
pieces.blurb: The log has every write, so search it.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: The WAL isn’t indexed, and that segment was already deleted after the flush.

pieces.title: Bloom filter says yes, so return without reading
pieces.blurb: If the filter matches, the key is there.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: A Bloom filter can give false positives. A match only means “maybe”; you still read the block.

pieces.title: Open all 212 SSTables and search each
pieces.trapIfPlaced: That’s exactly what Bloom filters and indexes exist to avoid.

pieces.title: Overwrite the order’s page on disk
pieces.blurb: Write path: find the page, overwrite it.
